current.text: OKC traded away Lu Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins, mostly to save money, and took back no salary. Nobody was added to replace them except rookies and unproven young players.
The trades cut a projected luxury tax bill of 240 million USD to 20 million USD and brought in seven second-round picks.
The departures open up usage for the players who remain.
Even after these losses, the rotation stays deep.
Cason Wallace is almost certain to start. He is listed as the starting SG next to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein.
Guard minutes go to Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Wallace and Topic. Wallace and Mitchell both play a lot of minutes.
The Thunder will have to give more minutes to Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain.
Gilgeous-Alexander is doing more off-ball work. The need to get Mitchell and McCain on the floor may be the reason.
The team may get less elite on defense and lean more on offense, playing Gilgeous-Alexander, Mitchell and Jalen Williams together.
Jalen Williams and Alex Caruso are the only true wings left who can guard bigger forwards.
The centers in the rotation are Hartenstein, Holmgren and Jaylin Williams. Jaylin Williams barely played unless the centers were out.
The Thunder are unsure about Hartenstein's long-term future with the team.
The frontcourt is crowded. The June note lists Holmgren, Hartenstein, Jaylin Williams, the re-signed Al Horford and Thomas Sorber. That limits minutes for rookie big men right away.
Without Joe, Dort and Wiggins, OKC will not repeat last season's share of about 37% of its shots coming from three. Expect fewer team threes.
Ryland expects the team to push its core players to shoot more threes.
OKC has the best win total in the league. Ryland projects about 62 wins, with a range of 57 to 62, and has OKC and San Antonio as the top two seeds in the West. There is no tanking risk.
OKC has the fewest back-to-backs in the league, so its stars have less reason to rest.
The playoff schedule is good: 11 games in weeks 19 to 21 (rank 4 of 30), with only two back-to-back pairs.

durable.text: OKC's core players take very few threes.

note: OKC is the top contender. It has the fewest back-to-backs and a good playoff schedule, so Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the other starters carry little rest or tanking risk. The trades of Dort, Joe and Wiggins open minutes and usage for Cason Wallace (likely starter), Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain, while the crowded frontcourt limits rookie bigs like Aday Mara. Early on, watch how the guard minutes split among Mitchell, McCain and Topic, and whether Shai's extra off-ball work cuts his usage.
